sources.entry: Upkeep by wei18 - Upkeep — an AI audit crew for your repo. Catches docs/spec/asset drift with evidence; output-only. Claude Code plugin/skill + reusable CI workflow.

summary.one_liner: Upkeep is an AI audit tool that runs parallel AI reviewers over a whole repository to find semantic drift (stale docs, specs out of sync with code, orphaned assets, convention violations) and reports findings with evidence without editing files.
summary.what_it_does: Upkeep scans a repository and dispatches several focused AI reviewers in parallel, each covering one area such as docs staleness, spec/flow mismatches, duplicate or orphaned files, and repo conventions. It reports divergence with evidence and severity rather than assuming one artifact is the source of truth. It is output-only and never edits or deletes files. Results come as a self-contained HTML report and a terminal or chat summary. In CI it can maintain a single upserted GitHub tracking issue and upload the report as a workflow artifact. The engine runs on the user's machine using a logged-in claude CLI (Claude Pro/Max), with no separate API key.
use_cases: audit a repo for stale documentation
find specs that no longer match the code
scheduled repo-wide drift checks in CI
check translated READMEs for out-of-sync content
how_to_run: git clone --depth 1 <upkeep repo> ~/.cache/upkeep && cd ~/.cache/upkeep && npm ci
Add .github/workflows/audit.yml that uses wei18/upkeep/.github/workflows/audit.yml@v2 with the CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN secret
notable: Output-only design: reports drift with evidence and severity but never edits or deletes files
Runs on an existing Claude Pro/Max subscription instead of a per-token Anthropic API key
Parallel focused reviewers (docs, code hygiene, specs, visual/icons, duplicates/orphans, conventions, optional i18n)
CI mode upserts one GitHub tracking issue instead of creating duplicates
Configurable per repo via .claude/audit.yml; works as a Claude Code plugin, a skills.sh skill, a reusable workflow, a Marketplace action, or a plain script
caveats: Requires a logged-in claude CLI with a Pro/Max plan; CI needs a CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN secret generated via claude setup-token
The engine runs on the user's machine in every install mode, so it needs Node 20+ and git locally
The Marketplace action runs reviewers sequentially rather than in parallel; the README recommends the reusable workflow instead
The @v1 reusable workflow tag is frozen; users must move to @v2
keywords: check my repo for outdated docs
